name: writing-workspace-v1
purpose: Measure whether an engine release, document build, and visible workspace remain usable under real project scale without treating callback tests or historical green receipts as current acceptance.
law: Report cold and warm observations separately, including active-writer versus idle state.
Keep latency, payload bytes, browser render/interaction, provider context, and durable storage growth as separate measurements.
A passing owner/unit test is not a button acceptance; a successful HTTP response is not a rendered-page acceptance.
Measurements describe the tested project and host. They are reference observations, not universal performance budgets.
Never mutate a production manuscript merely to measure a read path; use an authorised real edit or a disposable fixture for mutation timing.

measure: service source identity, PID, active jobs and frontend bundle
HTTP TTFB, total time and response bytes for project shell, manuscript, Research, Figures, Formal targets, session list, session summary and exact detail
pre/post mutation owner-snapshot time and number of files hashed
Apply dependency replay count and elapsed time
journal and content-addressed-body bytes added by one no-op, one repeated body and one substantive change
owner-reported build state, elapsed time and active-job identity
selected root and dependency receipt currentness
exit status, compiler log and produced PDF SHA-256/bytes/pages
visible page and figure inspection for the changed range
whether a failed build leaves the prior current PDF distinguishable from the failed attempt
acceptance: The selected source builds through its owner and returns a terminal receipt.
The delivered PDF is current against the recorded dependency set.
The changed pages are visually inspected; source compilation alone is insufficient.

measure: cold project open and first useful content
warm click-to-visible-result for Manuscript, Research result, Figures, Formal target, History and saved conversation
network request fan-out per subview and whether closed disclosures trigger unrelated reads
DOM/accessibility node growth for long conversations and result catalogues
focus, scroll, Back/Escape, accepted-proposal terminal state and guarded Undo after reload
acceptance: Exercise actual controls in the delivered browser/native host, including empty, error, disabled and reconnected states.
Record browser latency separately from backend TTFB and accessibility-tree capture overhead.
Keep exact saved history reachable through lazy detail rather than rendering or deleting it eagerly.

measure: provider/model, advertised and effective context windows
last-turn input/cache/output tokens and cumulative input/cache/output tokens
initial operating brief, dynamic tool declarations, changed guidance, current context and explicit history retrieval as separate components when observable
provider_context.interpretation: Cached tokens are not new prompt bytes. Do not attribute the full cumulative input count to historical recursion without component evidence.
